- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often lags — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of prior day’s range to reflect sentiment reversal.
- If model shows steady upward drift with no sentiment support, it overestimates — apply mean reversion by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from forecast if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle volatility — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or bullish in last 3–5 days.
